short_description: 150 screen-free play cards for ages 1–12, sorted by age and energy, each with what you need, a talk prompt and a safety line. Plus summer and rainy-day sets.
long_description:
“I’m bored!” is where play begins. These 150 printable play cards turn that moment into something to do together, using things you already have: pots, socks, boxes, paper and the great outdoors.

Every card is sorted by age (1–3, 3–5, 5–8 and 8–12) and color-coded so you can find the right one at a glance. Each shows an energy level (calm, medium or wiggly), what you need, one or two short steps, a talk prompt to use while you play, and its own safety line. Every card for ages 1–3 uses only things bigger than a toilet-paper tube, and no card uses balloons.

You also get 36 bonus cards (18 summer, 18 rainy-day), 30 blank “your idea” cards, card backs in six colors, 18 box dividers, jar labels in four colorways (including calm, medium and wiggly jars), a velcro-ready Play Menu choice board, a weekly play planner with Monday and Sunday starts, a Play Jar Star certificate, a card index and a quick-answers page.

The download includes US Letter and A4 files, a fillable editable PDF for typing your own cards, a double-sided cards file, and a PNG template set for design apps. Printing, laminating and velcro tips are inside.

This is a digital file; nothing is shipped. For use in your own home.

compliance_notes: Rule 1: no health, medical, therapy, developmental or outcome claims anywhere; the FAQ and final page state the cards are parent education, not medical or developmental advice. No autism/ADHD/therapy/speech words in the product, images, keywords or tags. Rule 2: no company, app, device or product is named (fillable-PDF and design-app instructions are written generically; see human_todo about naming apps). Rule 4 child safety: all 186 cards were audited: adult supervision on every card (each has its own safety line); every Ages 1–3 card and every seasonal card that includes age 1 uses only objects larger than a toilet-paper tube and says so; older cards that use small items (coins, dice, tape, seeds, dough, shakers) carry a 'keep away from under-3s' line; no balloons anywhere; no cords, strings, ties or long scarves (sheets are 'draped, never tied'; masks are hand-held); every water activity says 'grown-up within arm's reach'; no whole grapes, nuts, popcorn, hard candy or marshmallows; grown-up handles knives, stove, oven, glass and tools; hide-and-seek card forbids appliances, chests, trunks and cars; outdoor cards keep play away from the street, no berries or mushrooms, sun and thunder rules. Rule 5: the only citation is WHO 2019 under-5 guidelines (180 minutes of varied physical activity for ages 1–4), an allowed source. Rule 6: talk strategies in plain words, no program names. Rule 7 and logo rules: original titles, art and layout; official logo files from brand/logo/ used unaltered on the cover, page headers, footers, card backs and labels (the logo motif restrictions apply to marks; the 'Hand Shadows' and 'Sock Puppet Hello' cards are activities, not marks). Copyright line on every page. Honest pricing: no anchor or 'was' price.
